title: Candidate Decline & Offer Debrief Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
--------
Purpose: Provide a clear, repeatable process for handling candidate declines and offer debriefs so the hiring team can close the loop with candidates quickly, extract actionable improvements, and feed structured data into recruitment metrics.
Scope: Applies to all full-time and contract candidate offers extended by Redwood Inference (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private teams). This playbook covers declines (candidate declines an offer) and withdrawals (candidate withdraws before offer acceptance).

Definitions
-----------
- Decline: Candidate formally rejects a written offer.
- Withdrawal: Candidate removes themselves from consideration prior to or during offer negotiation.
- Debrief: Structured meeting between recruiter, hiring manager, interviewers, and (when relevant) compensation or legal to record cause and next steps.

Owner & Roles
-------------
- Recruiting Owner: primary point-of-contact for candidate communications and ATS updates (Owner: Recruiting Team).
- Hiring Manager: leads technical/role debrief, decision owner for next steps.
- Interview Panel / Interviewer(s): provide panel feedback & interview notes.
- Compensation Partner: consulted if decline reason is compensation-related.
- People-ops Analytics: consumes taxonomy-coded decline reasons for quarterly analysis.

Process (timeline & actions)
---------------------------
1) Incident Window: 0–4 hours after decline notification
   - Recruiter acknowledges candidate message within 4 business hours.
   - If candidate provided a reason, capture verbatim in ATS note and set the ATS tag: DECLINE_RECEIVED.
   - Send an immediate, empathetic acknowledgement to candidate (template provided below).

2) Short Window: 4–48 hours
   - Recruiter flags Hiring Manager and schedules 30-minute debrief within 48 hours (calendar invite with context and links to ATS record and interview notes).
   - If candidate declines due to compensation, recruiter immediately pings Compensation Partner for feasibility review (response SLAs: 24 hours).

3) Debrief Meeting (within 48 hours of decline) — Agenda
   - 1. Read candidate decline verbatim.
   - 2. Confirm timeline: where in process did the decline occur (offer stage, negotiation, pre-offer withdrawal).
   - 3. Collect concrete reasons: Candidate verbatim reason and interviewer observations.
   - 4. Decide remediation actions: adjust JD/scope, update rubric, adjust comp band, re-open pipeline.
   - 5. Assign owner(s) and target dates for each remediation.
   - 6. Close loop with candidate if committed to follow-up (e.g., counteroffer fallback, future engagement).

4) Reporting & Retention (within 5 business days)
   - Recruiter completes the Offer Debrief Form (template below) and sets ATS final disposition to DECLINED + TAXONOMY code.
   - People-ops Analytics automatically ingests decline codes for weekly dashboards; recruiting manager reviews weekly exceptions.

Offer Debrief Form (template)
----------------------------
Use this template in the ATS or the Debrief Google Form. Capture each field exactly as shown:
- Candidate name: ____________
- Role / Team: ____________
- Hiring manager: ____________
- Recruiter: ____________
- Offer date (YYYY-MM-DD): ____________
- Decline / withdrawal date (YYYY-MM-DD): ____________
- Offer comp (total cash + equity / note if range): ____________
- Candidate-provided reason (verbatim): "___________________"
- Decline reason category (select one primary):
    * compensation
    * counteroffer from current employer
    * timing / notice period
    * role-scope mismatch
    * culture-fit / manager-perception
    * relocation / remote preference
    * personal/family reasons
    * visa/immigration
    * other (specify)
- Interview stage where decision made: (checkboxes) final-round, after offer, during negotiation, before offer
- Recruiter qualitative notes (2–4 bullets): ____________
- Remediation actions (owner + due date): e.g., update JD (owner: hiring manager, due: YYYY-MM-DD)
- Follow up to candidate? (yes/no) + message owner

Standard Templates
------------------
Internal acknowledgement to candidate (send within 4 hours):
"Hi <Candidate>, thanks for letting us know and for the time you invested with Redwood Inference. I appreciate your transparency — if youre open to sharing more about your decision, any details you provide will be kept confidential and used to improve our process. Best wishes, <Recruiter>"

Decline close-loop template (if follow-up committed):
"Hi <Candidate>, thank you again for the candid update. Per our conversation, Ill loop back by <date> with the items we discussed: [compensation feasibility / remote option / revised timeline]. If youd prefer not to hear follow-ups, let me know and we wont reach out. — <Hiring Manager / Recruiter>"

Salvage-language for counteroffers (manager tips):
- Focus on impact and growth opportunities instead of punitive comp comparisons.
- Highlight unique Redwood benefits (inference-scale projects, product ownership, Dedicated customer stories).
- Ask one open question: "What would make you seriously consider us again?" Avoid long justifications.

Taxonomy & Analytics (why structured coding matters)
--------------------------------------------------
- Use the exact decline reason codes from the Offer Debrief Form. People-ops Analytics maps codes to dashboards:
  * Weekly: top 5 decline reasons by hiring funnel stage.
  * Monthly: comp-related declines vs. market benchmark bands.
  * Quarterly: role-level retention risk (e.g., spikes in declines on a single manager/team).
- Key metrics to track: Offer acceptance rate, Time-to-offer, Decline reason distribution, Re-engagement rate within 12 months.

SLOs & SLA (recommended targets)
--------------------------------
- Acknowledge candidate decline: <= 4 business hours from recruiter.
- Schedule debrief: within 48 business hours.
- Debrief form completed: within 5 business days.
- Compensation feasibility response when requested: <= 24 business hours.

Data & Privacy Considerations
----------------------------
- Candidate verbatim reasons and personal details are PII. Retain debrief records in the ATS only according to Redwoods Data Retention policy: 2 years standard retention for declined candidates unless candidate requests deletion.
- If the decline cites health/medical/personal reasons, redact specifics from transmittable notes and mark the ATS record as "sensitive". Only Recruiting, Hiring Manager, and People-ops Analytics have access to sensitive tags.

Manager Checklist (post-debrief)
--------------------------------
1. Confirm remediation items were added to the team backlog and assigned.
2. Review interview rubric and surface any calibration items to Interview Calibration Channel.
3. Re-assess compensation band if comp was primary decline reason (engage Compensation Partner).
4. If decline suggests manager perception issues, request a skip-level calibration session with Eng L7+.
5. If more pipeline is needed, ask Recruiting to re-open active searches and prioritize 3 high-fit candidates within 10 business days.

Escalation & Exceptions
-----------------------
- If the same manager or job has 3+ declines in 90 days with the same primary reason, Recruiting Manager escalates to People-ops Partner for a joint review.
- If legal or immigration issues are cited, immediately loop in Legal (SLA: 24 hours) and tag record LEGAL_REVIEW.

Tracking & Quarterly Review
--------------------------
People-ops hosts a quarterly "Decline Insights" review with recruiting, hiring managers, and compensation to:
- Present aggregated decline reason trends and recommended actions.
- Surface role- or manager-specific patterns and agreed remediation.
- Update playbook and taxonomy as market conditions change.

Appendix A — Example Debrief (filled)
------------------------------------
- Candidate name: Samira Gomez
- Role: Backend Engineer, Runtime Team
- Hire manager: Marco Li
- Recruiter: Jordan Park
- Offer date: 2028-11-02
- Decline date: 2028-11-09
- Offer comp: $180k base, 10k equity grant (range 170–200k)
- Candidate reason: "Received internal counteroffer and will stay for relocation aid."
- Primary reason: counteroffer from current employer
- Remediation: add relocation flexibility note to role (owner: Marco Li, due: 2028-11-30)
- Follow up to candidate: No
